canonical_name: AA-LCR: Artificial Analysis Long Context Reasoning benchmark
release_source: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ArtificialAnalysis/AA-LCR (initial commit and dataset upload Aug 5, 2025); https://artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/artificial-analysis-long-context-reasoning
metric: pass@1 accuracy on 100 open-answer questions, graded by an LLM equality checker against reference answers
score_at_release_system: Not retrieved (site only states 'mid-2024 frontier models achieve less than 50% accuracy')
n_items: 100 questions over 30 document sets (234 documents, ~100k tokens per question)
lineage: Component of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (from 2025); AA-LCR v1.1 methodology: 'Adds a system prompt to clarify grading instructions, corrects 16 answer keys, and grades with GPT-5.6 Luna (medium)' (date not stated)
best_by_cutoff: 88.7%, Kimi K3 (Max), Artificial Analysis leaderboard (v1.1 methodology), accessed 2026-10-03, https://artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/artificial-analysis-long-context-reasoning ; next Step 5 Preview 88.3, MiMo-V2.6-Pro 86.3. Lab self-report max: Kimi K3 74.7 (2026-07-16, older grading)
notes: Human data: 'individual evaluators achieved modest accuracy rates, typically answering 40-60% of questions correctly on the first attempt'; every question answered correctly by at least one tester -> average human well below 85 -> criterion B, threshold 90. No result >= 90 by cutoff (AA top 88.7 as of 2026-10-03). Third-party benchmark with public questions and answers (Apache-2.0), so it is a public capability benchmark (main). v1.1 corrected 16% of answer keys and changed the grader - close to the codebook's >10% new-version rule, but labs keep the name, so treated as one unit; the change explains why AA's scores (e.g., Kimi K3 88.7) exceed earlier lab self-reports (74.7). Not an E event (maintainer fix, 16% < 20%).

canonical_name: AA-Omniscience: Evaluating Cross-Domain Knowledge Reliability in Large Language Models (Artificial Analysis)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.13029 (Nov 17, 2025); public split https://huggingface.co/datasets/ArtificialAnalysis/AA-Omniscience-Public (initial commit Nov 17, 2025)
metric: Omniscience Index = correct minus incorrect (hallucinated) answers, abstentions neutral; bounded -100 to 100 (accuracy and hallucination rate also reported)
score_at_release_system: Claude 4.1 Opus (index; 'one of only three models to score above zero')
n_items: 6000 questions over 42 topics in 6 domains (600 public in AA-Omniscience-Public, remainder held out)
lineage: Component of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (accuracy 10%, non-hallucination rate 5%); public 10% split released alongside; question update 2025-11-20
best_by_cutoff: Index 46, Claude Opus 5.5 (Max) (released 2026-09-22), then GPT-6 Astra (High) 44, Claude Fable 5.1 (Max) 43; best accuracy 67% (Claude Fable 5.1); Artificial Analysis leaderboard accessed 2026-10-03, https://artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/omniscience
notes: STRATUM JUDGEMENT: the index mixes factual recall (capability) with calibrated abstention; Anthropic reports it in system-card honesty/hallucination sections, which argues for 'propensity', but the creators frame it as a knowledge-reliability benchmark with a hard ceiling (100 = all answered correctly), like negative-marked exams, so coded main. Scale is -100..100; criterion B threshold taken literally as 90% of the scale maximum = 90 index points (if 90% of the full range were used instead: 80). No human baseline. Far from threshold at cutoff (top 46). Anthropic self-reports in the input carry no numbers.

No later lab reports found (Qwen3-Omni 2025-09 and Qwen3-VL 2025-11 reports do not include it; not in Gemini 3 / Kimi / Muse materials per input data) -> >15 months without lab reports by 2026-09-30. No official leaderboard (GitHub repo only ships an eval script; last commit 2020-01); Papers-with-Code leaderboards closed 2025-07.
score_at_release_system: E-SA (creators' baseline; overall accuracy on test, AAAI 2019 paper)
n_items: 8,000 QA pairs on 800 test videos (train 32,000 / val 18,000 / test 8,000; 58,000 total)
lineage: Built on ActivityNet v1.3 videos (2015); sibling VideoQA sets MSVD-QA/MSRVTT-QA/TGIF-QA; LMM-era GPT-assisted scoring protocol from Video-ChatGPT (2023-06). No official successor.
best_by_cutoff: ~67: PLM-8B 67.3 (Meta PerceptionLM, LLM-judge accuracy, arXiv 2504.13180, 2025-04); Gemini 2.5 Pro 66.7 (visual-only, Gemini 2.5 tech report 2025-06-17)

Scoring protocol drift (exact match vs LLM judge) makes cross-paper numbers only roughly comparable. Abandonment judged on lab reports + absence of any official leaderboard; academic video-LLM papers may still cite it (not leaderboard activity). Test answers public since 2019-05 (commit 'add test_a.json').

release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.06364 (arXiv id 2304 = Apr 2023); data/repo https://github.com/ruixiangcui/AGIEval (first commits 2023-03-26)
metric: average accuracy over tasks (MCQ accuracy; EM for cloze tasks in v1.0); v1.1 leaderboard averages MCQ tasks only (AGIEval-en / -zh / -all)
score_at_release_system: GPT-4, few-shot chain-of-thought, average over tasks (zero-shot CoT 58.4)

lineage: Built from Gaokao, SAT, LSAT, LogiQA, JEC-QA, AQuA-RAT and MATH exam/competition items; v1.1 data and leaderboard revision 2024-06 (repo commits 2024-06-07/13); English MCQ subset 'AGIEval English' used by Meta, Google (T5Gemma 2) and Mistral

Still reported in 2025-2026 (Kimi K2, DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, T5Gemma 2), so alive. v1.1 (2024-06) revised items and made the leaderboard MCQ-only; treated as the same unit.

metric: answer accuracy (%)

ab_mode: few-shot, greedy decoding; LM writes reasoning chain/program executed by external solver (Python)

score_at_release_system: UnitDep (statistical MWP solver), 5-fold cross-validation on full ASDiv (LCA++ 36, GTS 36; ASDiv-A subset best 78)
lineage: Built in response to earlier MWP corpora (MAWPS, Math23K-style); ASDiv-A arithmetic subset (used to build SVAMP, 2021-03); used in CoT-era LLM evaluations (Wei et al. CoT 2022-01, PaLM 2022-04, PAL 2022-11, Toolformer 2023-02, Llama 2 2023-07, DeepSeek-Coder PAL 2023-11).

notes: No human baseline in the paper (only says SOTA systems are 'not competitive with human performance') -> criterion B, threshold 90. No official test split: the paper used 5-fold CV; LLM papers evaluate on the whole set or filtered versions (2,096 in CoT-style setups; 2,215 in ToRA). AB coded in main mode with a solver-backed scaffold because ASDiv's protocol (MWP solvers that output equations/answers) does not exclude computation tools; if tools were excluded, the first >=90 tool-free result found is GPT-4 CoT 91.3 (2023-09). Pre-GPT-4 bests were below 90 (e.g., code-davinci-002 with self-consistency/verifiers ~88). Strict: ToRA's paper does not state explicitly that its GPT-4 numbers are its own runs, but they are not OpenAI numbers (third-party), so treated as independent. Contamination: Anthropic engineering post 'Eval awareness in Claude Opus 4.6's BrowseComp performance' (2026-03-06) found 11/1,266 problems answered from leaked benchmark materials (incl. the model decrypting the canary-XOR answer key from GitHub) — <1% of items, not coded as E; Anthropic adopted blocklists. simple-evals repo deprecation notice (July 2025) keeps BrowseComp reference implementation, not a C event. Search for earlier non-lab >=90 claims (agent startups) limited to llm-stats aggregator (67 models) since WebSearch unavailable.

UNCERTAINTIES: (1) the official leaderboard at https://www.cybergym.io/cybergym/ is rendered by JavaScript; its data source could not be located and GitHub issue/API access was not available -> leaderboard entries (agent systems) unverified, source unreachable; (2) Google's Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber post (2026-09-02, trusted-defender-only model) reports CyberGym Pass@1 only in a chart image ('surpasses both 3.5 Flash Cyber as well as significantly larger frontier models'); the number could not be read -> if it was >=90, AB would be 2026-09. No C event: lastexam.ai news and the HLE-Diamond blog (2026-09-22) do not deprecate HLE or name saturation. Tool-assisted results (e.g., Grok 4 Heavy 50.7 in 2025-07) excluded per no-tools protocol.

Primary event is C: the creators (now at Edison Scientific/FutureHouse) cite saturation or superhuman performance on some LAB-Bench subsets as the reason for the harder LABBench2. The statement is partial (some subsets 'still being difficult'). Human baselines were measured with internet and tools, while model evals were mostly tool-free; Anthropic's FigQA 'with tools' numbers would not count under a no-tools reading. canonical_name: LAMBADA (LAnguage Modeling Broadened to Account for Discourse Aspects)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.06031 (arXiv id 1606 = submitted 2016-06; ACL 2016)
metric: accuracy of predicting the passage's final word (perplexity also reported; accuracy is the bounded primary measure)
abandoned_evidence: Last 9-lab report found: Google T5Gemma, released 2025-07-09 (https://developers.googleblog.com/en/t5gemma/). Its technical paper (https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.06225, v1 2025-04-08) reports Lambada for the Gemma 2 and T5Gemma pretrained models (Gemma 2 9B 76.6, T5Gemma 9B-9B 75.2). No later 9-lab release reports LAMBADA: T5Gemma 2 (2025-12, arXiv 2512.14856) dropped it; Gemma 3 (2025-03), Gemma 3n (2025-06), Gemma 3 270M (2025-08), VaultGemma (2025-09), Gemma 4 (2026-03) and Kimi Linear (2025-10) do not report it. That leaves >=14 months without reports before the 2026-09-30 cutoff. No official leaderboard exists. Earlier mentions: GPT-4o System Card 2024-08 (audio-converted LAMBADA, no score in text); Qwen-14B 71.1 (2023-09)
score_at_release_system: baseline 'random capitalized word from passage' (best trained model: N-gram w/ cache 0.1% accuracy, ppl 768)
n_items: 5153 (test passages; dev 4,869)
lineage: No official successor; an audio-converted version was used in the GPT-4o System Card (2024-08) voice-input tests
best_by_cutoff: 89.7 - PaLM 540B, 8-shot (2022-04, https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.02311 Table 4; prior few-shot SOTA 87.2, 15-shot)
notes: No measured human accuracy. Passages were kept only if two subjects guessed the target word from the full passage and the word was then not guessed by up to 10 further subjects who saw only the last sentence, so human success is ~100% by construction -> degenerate baseline -> criterion B (90% accuracy). The paper reports accuracy as the measure of interest; perplexity is unbounded and not used. No result >=90 found by the cutoff: GPT-3 few-shot 86.4 (2020-05, input lab report), prior few-shot SOTA 87.2 (15-shot) cited in the PaLM paper, PaLM 540B few-shot 89.7 (2022-04), PaLM 2-L 1-shot 86.9 (2023-05), Chinchilla 0-shot 77.4, Qwen-14B 71.1 (2023-09) (input lab reports). The search for later >=90 results was limited (no web search; papers/model cards only). Abandoned: no 9-lab release reports for >=12 months before the cutoff and no leaderboard. The input lab-report list stops at 2024-08 but misses Google's Gemma-family reports. The last LAMBADA activity found is T5Gemma: paper 2025-04, release 2025-07; I used the release month, and the paper month would give 2025-04. Hugging Face model cards (e.g., Mistral, Meta MobileLLM) could not be checked because huggingface.co is blocked, so a later report cannot be ruled out. The best >=90 search also covered T5Gemma, where Gemma 2 9B scores 76.6. The first lab report in the input is GPT-2 (2019-02), which gives a perplexity of 8.63.

Creators (Redwood post): 'We believe it is important for sabotage evals not to saturate quickly ... performance hasn't plateaued'; paper: human LaStraj attacks evade monitors at much higher rates, 'current attack policies do not saturate LinuxArena'. lineage: Aggregates earlier datasets (AddSub 2014, SingleOp, SingleEq 2015, MultiArith 2015, SimulEq/ALG514 2014); related successors ASDiv (2020), SVAMP (2021, built from ASDiv-A/MAWPS-style problems to expose shallow heuristics), GSM8K (2021).
best_by_cutoff: Not established as a single comparable number (protocols differ). Supervised: 92.0 RoBERTa-DeductReasoner (2022-03). Lab reports: DeepSeek-Coder 93.3 with PAL (program-aided, uses code execution; 2023-11); Llama 2-Chat with calculator (Toolformer protocol) 82.4 (2023-07).
notes: No human baseline -> B (90). Protocol heterogeneity is the main judgement call: the paper defines an official 80/20 split, but subsequent supervised work uses 5-fold CV on a filtered subset and LLM papers evaluate assorted MAWPS sub-datasets; AB taken on the dominant supervised-MWP protocol (as in Papers-with-Code 'MAWPS' table). Chain-of-thought paper v1 (2022-01) reported MAWPS sub-datasets separately (SingleOp/SingleEq/AddSub/MultiArith), not an aggregate, so not counted. PAL / tool-integrated numbers excluded from main mode (code execution). Prior SOTA before AB: Roberta-Graph2Tree 88.7 (Patel et al., 2021). Strict event not established (no independent re-run >=90 located). Labs stopped reporting after 2023-11 (DeepSeek Coder) - after the AB event, so not 'abandoned'.

best_by_cutoff: 91.8 - ERNIE-M large, translate-train-all (EMNLP 2021, https://aclanthology.org/2021.emnlp-main.3.pdf Table 4; arXiv 2012.15674, 2020-12); VECO large 91.1. notes: The PAWS-X paper reports no human performance on the task: the only humans mentioned are the translators and validators. XTREME (ICML 2020) lists human 97.5 for PAWS-X, but says it is taken from the English source dataset (PAWS), so it was not measured on the PAWS-X split -> criterion B (90). Metric convention: average accuracy over 7 test languages incl. English (XTREME and FILTER convention); the paper's own headline average covers the 6 non-English languages. Translate-train / 'Merged' training with the released machine-translated training data is a standard setting defined in the PAWS-X paper itself, so such results count. Earlier bests below 90: XTREME translate-train multi-task mBERT 88.9 (2020-03); X-STILTs (Phang et al., AACL 2020, arXiv 2005) 88.2; XLM-R zero-shot 86.4. date_upper_bound=1 because FILTER claims new state of the art on the XTREME leaderboard benchmark, and that unreadable leaderboard may have listed FILTER or another >=90 entry before the arXiv v1. Strict not coded: no organizer-verified or independently run single-model result >=90 could be documented (XTREME leaderboard unreadable; PAWS-X test labels are public). Lab usage is only Qwen (2024-02 to 2024-12, 5-shot base models) with no individual PAWS-X scores in the input.

Lab reports of the original PIQA run to 2024-12 (DeepSeek-V3); the 2025-2026 'Global PIQA' lab reports belong to a different benchmark.

release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.04683 (arXiv id 1704 = Apr 2017); EMNLP 2017 paper https://aclanthology.org/D17-1082.pdf

canonical_name: SimpleQA: Measuring short-form factuality in large language models (OpenAI; Wei et al.)
release_source: https://openai.com/index/introducing-simpleqa/ (2024-10-30); arXiv 2411.04368 v1 2024-11-07
metric: Correct (% of all 4,326 questions graded CORRECT by the prompted ChatGPT grader), closed-book/no browsing. This is the creators' headline number (blog chart Correct/Not attempted/Incorrect; openai/simple-evals 'SimpleQA' column = overall correct). Paper also offers F-score (harmonic mean of correct and correct-given-attempted) as an optional single number.
score_at_release_system: OpenAI o1-preview, no browsing (Correct 42.7; F-score 44.8); GPT-4o 38.2, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 28.9
lineage: Successors/variants: Chinese SimpleQA (Alibaba, arXiv 2411.07140, 2024-11; separate benchmark); BrowseComp (OpenAI, 2025-04-10; browsing successor); SimpleQA Verified (Google DeepMind, arXiv 2509.07968, 2025-09; 1,000 cleaned items, F1 headline). Grader reused by SealQA etc.
best_by_cutoff: Closed-book (counted protocol): 62.5 — GPT-4.5 preview (OpenAI blog/simple-evals, 2025-02-27); no closed-book result >=90 found. Tool-assisted (not counted): 97.1 — DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp agentic search (github 2025-09-29); Grok 4 Fast with search 95.0 (2025-09-19).
notes: Standard protocol is closed-book: blog says OpenAI measured 'several OpenAI models without browsing'; SimpleQA Verified paper also states tools give near-perfect performance and must not be used. Tool-assisted >=90 results therefore NOT counted for AB: earliest found Perplexity Deep Research 93.9% (perplexity.ai blog 2025-02-14); OpenAI GPT-4o Search Preview 90.0 (2025-03); ChatGPT agent 91.4 (2025-07-17); DeepSeek-V3.1 search agent 93.4 (2025-08-21). No human performance baseline: the 94.4% is a third AI trainer's agreement in the data-quality check (est. ~3% label error), not a baseline. JUDGEMENT CALL (C rejected): OpenAI's BrowseComp post (2025-04-10) says 'Existing benchmarks like SimpleQA, which measure models' ability to retrieve basic isolated facts, are already saturated by models with access to fast browsing tools, such as GPT-4o with browsing.' Not coded as C because the saturation claim is explicitly about the tool-assisted (non-counting) protocol and OpenAI kept reporting closed-book SimpleQA afterwards (GPT-5 system card 2025-08, gpt-oss-safeguard 2025-10-29); if adjudicators read it as C, c_date=2025-04, source https://openai.com/index/browsecomp/. E not coded: SimpleQA Verified (Google, 2025-09) reports noisy labels/redundancy and drops 76.9% of items, but mostly for de-duplication, publisher and topic balancing; removals for source conflicts are 8.3% + 3.9% of the remaining pool, so a >=20% defect rate is not documented, although Google, Anthropic, DeepSeek and Meta moved to SimpleQA Verified from 2025-11. Lab-report parsing: C-SimpleQA/CSimpleQA lines (DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen) are Chinese SimpleQA, a different benchmark; 'Hallucination rate' lines are a lower-is-better sub-metric. Last report of original SimpleQA by a listed lab: 2025-10-29 (OpenAI gpt-oss-safeguard), <12 months before cutoff, so not abandoned.

release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.05250 (arXiv id 1606 = Jun 2016); v1.1 leaderboard page introduced 2016-08-24 (commit 381e85d 'Update index for v1.1', https://github.com/rajpurkar/SQuAD-explorer)

ab_source: https://rajpurkar.github.io/SQuAD-explorer/ (v1.1 leaderboard; entry created 2018-09-27 per out-v1.1.json in https://github.com/rajpurkar/SQuAD-explorer)
strict_system: BERT (single model), Google AI Language
c_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.03822 (SQuAD 2.0 paper by the SQuAD creators, Rajpurkar, Jia & Liang)
c_quote: 'Recent work has even produced systems that surpass human-level exact match accuracy on the Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD)... One root cause of these problems is SQuAD's focus on questions for which a correct answer is guaranteed to exist in the context document.' (motivation for SQuAD 2.0, which replaced 1.1 as the main leaderboard)
score_at_release_system: Logistic regression with hand-engineered features (authors' baseline; test F1 51.0 / EM 40.4)
n_items: Hidden test, ~10% of 536 articles (exact question count not published); public dev 10,570 questions / 48 articles; train 87,599
lineage: v1.0 with paper (2016-06) -> v1.1 leaderboard (2016-08); successor SQuAD 2.0 (2018-06); derivatives Adversarial SQuAD (2017-07), QNLI in GLUE (2018-04), XQuAD (2019-10)
best_by_cutoff: F1 95.719 / EM 90.622, {ANNA} (single model), LG AI Research, leaderboard entry 2021-07-24 (last v1.1 entry), https://rajpurkar.github.io/SQuAD-explorer/
notes: Human performance = second crowd answer treated as prediction vs the other answers (single human). Paper (v1.0) reported test 77.0 EM / 86.8 F1, but the official v1.1 leaderboard (since 2016-08-28) shows creators' human performance 82.304 EM / 91.221 F1 on the v1.1 test -> used 91.221 F1 (>=85) -> criterion A. F1 chosen as primary (paper headline metric; leaderboard sorts by EM+F1). Sensitivities: (a) paper threshold 86.8 F1 -> first crossing 2017-11-18, BiDAF+Self-Attention+ELMo ensemble (87.432); (b) EM as primary: human EM 82.304 < 85 -> B (90 EM) -> LUKE single 90.202 EM, 2020-04-11; the famous 'beats human EM' entries were r-net+ ensemble 82.650 EM (2018-01-04) and first single MARS 82.587 (2018-05-09). nlnet ensemble 91.202 F1 on 2018-09-09 was just below 91.221. JUDGEMENT: C event coded from the SQuAD 2.0 paper (same creators) citing human-level EM on SQuAD and its answerability guarantee as the motivation for the successor; if C is not accepted, primary = AB 2018-09. Leaderboard dates = CodaLab submission 'created' timestamps from the repo JSON (displayed on the leaderboard). Lab LLM reports are not on the official test; moreover Meta's Llama 3.x 'SQuAD' numbers (85.6-89.3 EM, 1-shot) are SQuAD v2 per Meta's eval_details ('we use SQuAD v2 with a 1-shot config and report exact match', https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models/blob/main/models/llama3_1/eval_details.md), i.e. mis-mapped to this unit in the input.

exclusion_reason: Measures truthfulness, i.e. the tendency to avoid imitative falsehoods. The creators' primary objective is '% of answers that are true', and non-committal answers ('I have no comment') count as true, so the metric can be maximised by abstaining (README). Labs file it under safety/honesty: Llama 2 next to ToxiGen/BOLD, Claude 2 under honesty. Inverse scaling with model size in the original paper.

metric: Generation (main task): % true (primary) and % true-and-informative (secondary), judged by humans or fine-tuned GPT-judge; MC1/MC2 multiple-choice variants; binary-choice variant added Jan 2025
human_baseline: 94 (% true); 87 (% true and informative) — one participant, 250 randomly sampled questions, ~2 min/question, internet allowed
score_at_release_system: GPT-3 175B, helpful prompt (% true; 21% true-and-informative)

notes: JUDGEMENT CALL (stratum). Coded as propensity because the README defines the primary objective as % true and admits it 'can be gamed with a model that responds "I have no comment" to every question'. If adjudicated as main: primary metric = % true (generation), human baseline 94 on a 250-question random sample of the same set, so criterion A with threshold 94 (or 87 if % true-and-informative is taken as primary); MC1/MC2 have no human baseline, so B=90. Event research was not done, per the instruction to stop at identification for non-main strata. Jan 2025 authors' update is not a C event: old MC results are declared 'still valid'. Lab-report parsing: GPT-4o 81.4 is MC accuracy on English Translated TruthfulQA; Llama 2-Chat 64.14 and Code Llama 34.64/47.37 are % true-and-informative; InstructGPT 0.712 is % true with QA prompt.

Codebook rule 1.6 would make WMDP-Bio/Chem/Cyber separate units if the study splits them.

canonical_name: WorldVQA: Measuring Atomic World Knowledge in Multimodal Large Language Models (Zhou et al., Moonshot AI, 2026)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02537 (v1 submitted 2026-01-28); also announced as 'Moonshot-released benchmark' in Kimi K2.5 README (https://github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-K2.5, initial commit 2026-01-30); dataset repo https://github.com/MoonshotAI/WorldVQA (initial commit 2026-02-03)
metric: accuracy (% correct, LLM-judged by gpt-oss-120b; CGA and F-score secondary); headline leaderboard uses 8 categories excluding 'People'
score_at_release_system: Gemini-3-Pro (Kimi K2.5 46.3); paper: 'No model surpasses the 50% threshold'
n_items: 3500 VQA pairs (9 categories; ~3,000 in headline 8-category score)
lineage: Visual analogue of SimpleQA-style factuality benchmarks; created by Moonshot AI; no successor found. Variant: 'WorldVQA ForceAnswer' (Kimi K3 README, 2026-07).
best_by_cutoff: 61.1 - Qwen3.7-Plus, 2026-06-01 (Qwen blog per lab_reports, not verified: qwen.ai JS-rendered; setting unclear); verified: Kimi K3 51.0 (ForceAnswer), Claude Fable 5 56.7 (ForceAnswer, Moonshot-run), Kimi-K3 README 2026-07.
notes: No human baseline in paper -> criterion B. Answers graded by LLM judge (gpt-oss-120b; 98.1% agreement with humans on 160-sample audit). Human annotators wrote QA pairs from web-sourced images (LLM-in-the-loop expansion for coverage), deduplicated vs LAION/Common Crawl. All reported scores (46-61) far below 90. Benchmark is created by a reporting lab (Moonshot). Lab reports: Kimi K2.5 46.3 (2026-01), Qwen3.7-Plus 61.1 (2026-06), Kimi K3 ForceAnswer 51.0 (2026-07), Qwen3.8-Max 53.2 (2026-08).

canonical_name: WritingBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Generative Writing (Wu et al., Alibaba / X-PLUG)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.05244 (v1 2025-03-07); github.com/X-PLUG/WritingBench README '2025-03-10 We release the first version of WritingBench, including 1,239 writing queries'
metric: mean rubric score: 5 query-specific criteria per query, each scored 1-10 by a judge (paper: fine-tuned Qwen-7B critic; leaderboard: Claude-3.7-Sonnet from 2025-04-29, Claude-Sonnet-4 from 2025-09-05, Claude-Sonnet-4.5 from 2025-11-27). Leaderboard multiplies by 10 (0-100).
score_at_release_system: DeepSeek-R1, critic-model judge, original 1,239-query version (arXiv v1 Table 3; Qwen-Max 8.37, ChatGPT-4o-latest 8.16)
n_items: 1000 (since 2025-04-29 revision; originally 1,239)
lineage: v1 2025-03 (1,239 queries, critic model) -> 2025-04-29 revision (1,000 queries, new criteria/prompt, Claude-3.7-Sonnet judge, HF/ModelScope leaderboard) -> judge switched to Claude-Sonnet-4 (2025-09-05) and Claude-Sonnet-4.5 (2025-11-27). No renamed successor.
best_by_cutoff: 88.3 — Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507 (Qwen HF card self-report 2025-07-25, Claude-3.7 judge era). Official leaderboard (Sonnet-4.5 judge, imported 2026-05-28 by benchmarklist.com): top gpt-5-2025-08-07 83.87; LongCat 2.0 83.8 (2026-07-20).
notes: Scale: leaderboard 0-100 (raw 10-point score x10), so threshold 90 = 9.0 raw. No human answering baseline; human annotators only validated judge agreement (83%), so B. Nothing >=90 under any judge/version. VERSION CALL: the 2025-04-29 revision changed >10% of items (1,239 -> 1,000 with updated criteria) and the judge, so under codebook rule 1.2 it could be its own unit with birth 2025-04; coded here as one family unit (unversioned name in all lab reports) with birth at first release (2025-03). Qwen3 tech report's 8.03 (2025-05) is on the raw 10-point scale; later Qwen numbers (85.2, 88.3, 87.3) use the leaderboard 100-point scale. Scores across judge changes are not comparable. Lab reports continued past the input list (Qwen3-VL series 2025-09/10; repo and leaderboard updates to 2025-12; leaderboard snapshot 2026-05), so not abandoned.

canonical_name: XCOPA: A Multilingual Dataset for Causal Commonsense Reasoning (Ponti et al., EMNLP 2020)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.00333 (arXiv id 2005 = May 2020); data in https://github.com/cambridgeltl/xcopa (commits from 2020-04-27, README updates 2020-05-01)
metric: accuracy averaged over 11 languages (2-way choice)
ab_mode: 4-shot, no chain-of-thought
ab_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10403 (PaLM 2 Technical Report, 2023-05-10: 'establishes a new state of the art even without chain-of-thought prompting')
score_at_release_system: RoBERTa-large, translate-test (authors' best; XLM-R Large zero-shot transfer 68.69)
n_items: 5500 test (500 per language x 11 languages); validation 100 per language
lineage: Translation and re-annotation of English COPA (Roemmele et al., 2011; also in SuperGLUE 2019) into 11 languages; reported by Qwen (2024) inside multilingual averages
best_by_cutoff: 94.4, PaLM 2-L 4-shot (2023-05-10, PaLM 2 Technical Report); later lab reports (Qwen1.5-2.5) only give multilingual group averages
notes: The README 'Human' row (avg 97.60) is the share of each translator's labels that agree with the majority label of the 11 translators ('We then compute the percentage of annotated labels which agree with the majority label'), assigned on the English premise during translation - an agreement statistic in which each translator is part of the majority, not humans solving the translated test; parent COPA's human baseline is degenerate (100%). Treated as degenerate -> criterion B, threshold 90. Sensitivity under A (97.6): no known result reaches it (max 94.4). Before PaLM 2: PaLM-540B EN-CoT 89.9 (Shi et al., arXiv 2210.03057, Oct 2022), just below 90; direct 83.7. XCOPA test labels are public, so results are self-reported; strict left blank (no organizer-verified or independent single-model run >= 90 found). Leaderboard = README table/Papers with Code (no hidden test).

canonical_name: XWinograd: multilingual Winograd schema collection (Tikhonov & Ryabinin, Findings ACL 2021; extended by Muennighoff et al. 2022)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.12066 (arXiv id 2106 = Jun 2021); extended version used by labs: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Muennighoff/xwinograd (Muennighoff et al., arXiv 2211.01786, Nov 2022)
metric: accuracy (2-way pronoun/candidate choice), per language; no official aggregate - coded as average over en/fr/jp/pt/ru/zh
abandoned_evidence: Only lab user is Alibaba/Qwen, and only inside an aggregated multilingual 'Understanding' score; last report = Qwen2.5 Technical Report 2024-12-19. No lab report found afterwards (T5Gemma 2 and Gemma 4 cards omit it) and the dataset has no leaderboard, so >=12 months without reports or leaderboard activity before 2026-09-30.
score_at_release_system: Original paper evaluated attention-head baselines on mBERT/XLM-R (numbers not retrieved); BLOOMZ paper (2022-11) reports ~60-72% per language for BLOOMZ-7.1B / mT0-13B
n_items: 4449 test examples in the Muennighoff version (en 2,325; fr 83; jp 959; pt 263; ru 315; zh 504); test-only, no train/dev
lineage: Built from existing Winograd schema collections (WSC273/WSC variants and translations) by Tikhonov & Ryabinin (2021-06); Chinese part expanded from 16 to 504 items with CLUE WSC2020 by Muennighoff et al. (2022-11, BLOOMZ/xP3 held-out eval); used by Qwen1.5-2.5 (2024)
best_by_cutoff: No per-dataset frontier numbers found; Qwen publishes only group averages (e.g., Qwen2-72B 'Understanding' 80.7 incl. Belebele/XCOPA/XWinograd/XStoryCloze/PAWS-X); BLOOMZ paper best ~70+% (mT0-13B)
notes: No creators' human baseline -> criterion B, threshold 90. No public result >= 90 (average or headline) found; frontier LLMs might exceed 90 on the English part but nobody reports it as XWinograd. Language subsets are not translations of each other and differ greatly in size, so 'average' is my operationalization. Web search budget was exhausted while coding this unit, so the search for high-scoring third-party results was limited (WebFetch on known papers only). If the extended version (Nov 2022, +488 Chinese items) is treated as the unit, birth would be 2022-11.

canonical_name: ZebraLogic (logic grid puzzles; AI2/UW; HF blog 2024-07, ICML 2025 paper 'On the Scaling Limits of LLMs for Logical Reasoning')
release_source: HF leaderboard space allenai/ZebraLogic initial commits 2024-07-11 (huggingface.co/spaces/allenai/ZebraLogic/commits/main); blog https://huggingface.co/blog/yuchenlin/zebra-logic (July 2024); arXiv 2502.01100 v1 2025-02-03
metric: puzzle-level accuracy (% of 1,000 puzzles with every cell correct), greedy decoding; cell-level accuracy is secondary
ab_mode: greedy, single run (pass@1)
ab_source: Official ZeroEval/ZebraLogic leaderboard: github.com/WildEval/ZeroEval commit c86a194 'add o3 mini results' 2025-04-01 (result_dirs/zebra-grid.summary.json: Puzzle Acc 91.70); HF space allenai/ZebraLogic summary update 2025-04-01
strict_system: o3-mini-2025-01-31-high, evaluated by the benchmark organizers
score_at_release_system: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (2024-06-20), per the July 2024 blog ('can only solve 33.4% of all puzzles')
lineage: Part of AI2's ZeroEval suite (with WildBench). Paper version 2025-02 (same 1,000 puzzles, adds Z3 search-space analysis). Successor/variant: MultiZebraLogic (arXiv 2511.03553, multilingual).
best_by_cutoff: 97.3 — Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Thinking (Alibaba self-report, 2025-09; via llm-stats); official leaderboard top grok-3-mini-fast-beta-high 92.6 (ZeroEval commit 2025-04-14).
notes: Leaderboard history (git log of result_dirs/zebra-grid.summary.json): top was o1-mini 46.7 (2024-09-13), o1-preview 71.4 (2024-10-22), o1-2024-12-17 81.0 (2025-01-21, also in arXiv v1 2025-02-03), then o3-mini-high 91.7 (2025-04-01), the first >=90; grok-3-mini-fast-beta-high 92.6 followed (2025-04-14). No earlier >=90 found in papers or lab reports (Qwen3 thinking 80.3 in 2025-05; Kimi K2 89.0 and Qwen3-2507 95.0 in 2025-07). No human baseline; blog gives only the author's solve times. Puzzles are generated programmatically (curation synthetic/templated).

canonical_name: ZeroBench: An Impossible Visual Benchmark for Contemporary Large Multimodal Models (Roberts et al., 2025)
metric: accuracy on 100 main questions with 5 samples: pass@5 (any correct) and pass^5 (all 5 correct, 'reliability'); mean pass@1 also on leaderboard; 334 subquestions scored separately ('ZeroBench-Sub')
score_at_release_system: all frontier LMMs at release (adversarially filtered); v3: 'SotA pass@5 score increased from 5%->19% (Gemini 3 Pro)'
n_items: 100 main questions (334 subquestions)
lineage: Same group's earlier difficult visual benchmarks; no successor found. Variants reported by labs: ZeroBench (w/ tools), ZeroBench-Sub (subquestions).
best_by_cutoff: pass@5 52.0 / pass^5 35.0 / pass@1 43.2 - GPT-6 Astra (max), official leaderboard https://zerobench.github.io/ (Astra released 2026-09-03); with tools: GPT-5.6 Sol pass@5 54.6 (externally reported per leaderboard); DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash w/ tools pass@5 49 (2026-09-10, self).
notes: Human baseline in v3 paper: 29.5±27.1% (mean of 15 undergraduate/postgraduate evaluators on the 100 main questions) -> below 85% -> criterion B, threshold 90. Standard protocol is without tools; tool-assisted results (Kimi K2.5 11, Muse Spark 33, DeepSeek 35/49, Kimi K3 41) noted only. Lab reports mix pass@5 on main questions and subquestion accuracy (Qwen3.5 ZEROBench_sub 41.0; Qwen3.8-Max ZeroBench-Sub 48.5) - different metric. All results far below 90 at cutoff; official leaderboard is maintained and active (includes GPT-6 Sol/Astra, Claude Opus 5.5).
